strengths: Addresses important AI safety problem of deception evasion when training against detectors
Realistic experimental setup with naturally-occurring reward hacking in MBPP coding tasks, more convincing than artificial toy settings
Comprehensive empirical investigation across 4 models, multiple probes, systematic hyperparameter sweeps, and extensive ablations
Clear conceptual framework: decomposition (Eq. 3) elegantly explains how different policy classes achieve high reward
Novel policy gradient theory (Appendix D) proving standard methods don't backprop through probes, explaining representation drift origin
Creative characterization of three distinct obfuscated policy strategies with concrete examples
Promising result that honest policies can match best unconstrained baselines in capabilities (Figure 5)
Excellent presentation with clear writing and well-designed visualizations; comprehensive appendices support reproducibility; code/models released
weaknesses: Severe domain limitation: all experiments restricted to MBPP coding tasks; generalization to other RLVR domains (mathematical reasoning, chemistry, software development) completely unexplored, drastically limiting impact

Core solution impractical: achieving honest policies requires β≥0.1 (high KL regularization) which practitioners avoid due to performance degradation; no solutions provided for real-world applications with lower KL

Obfuscated policies undetectable at deployment: paper acknowledges these are 'harder to detect and require inspecting outputs for unusual patterns' but provides no automated detection mechanism, creating deployment-time vulnerabilities
Representation drift explanation lacks rigor: relies on belief probing with 20 ad-hoc questions to infer model beliefs, which is intuitive but not principled; alternative explanations not explored

Limited theoretical understanding: Equation 3 explains why strategies exist but lacks formal conditions for when high β+high α yields honesty vs. obfuscation; no convergence analysis or characterization of thresholds

Detector training circularity: detectors trained on off-domain synthetic deception may not capture real obfuscation strategies learned during RLVR training; no validation that these are relevant deception directions
Surprising negative result inadequately explained: Appendix L shows continual detector retraining doesn't reduce obfuscation, raising fundamental questions about off-domain detector effectiveness
Limited statistical rigor: only 3 seeds per configuration with large error bars in some results; no formal hypothesis tests or multiple comparison corrections; model-specific variation not explained

strengths: Realistic RLVR environment (MBPP-Honeypot) with naturally emerging reward hacking, going beyond prior toy settings
Clear four-outcome taxonomy with elegant mathematical decomposition (Equation 3) explaining each failure mode
Rigorous theoretical analysis (Appendix D) explaining why policy gradient methods don't optimize for activation obfuscation, with empirical validation
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across four models with systematic hyperparameter sweeps, extensive ablations, and multiple probe types
Mechanistic understanding of representation drift through belief probing (Appendix E), showing RLVR updates model beliefs about hardcoding
Detailed characterization of three obfuscated policy strategies with concrete examples and clear classification methodology
Practical insights showing detector penalties improve (not reduce) capabilities and establishing a clear 'safety region' (high KL + detector penalty)
Extensive reproducibility details across 21 appendices addressing implementation, ablations, and alternative settings
weaknesses: Limited environmental scope: only MBPP coding (simple hardcoding) and one supplementary non-coding task; generalization to more complex reward hacking and richer action spaces remains unclear
Critical reliance on KL regularization as primary solution, which practitioners often avoid due to task performance reduction; no principled guidance for setting β in new domains

Obfuscated policies remain undetectable at deployment (acknowledged limitation page 9): they evade detection through text changes, making them indistinguishable from honest policies without additional monitoring
Off-policy probe training shows poor generalization post-RLVR: off-domain probe AUC drops from ~0.99 to 0.38-0.66 (Table 4), raising scalability concerns as models become more capable
Model-dependent hyperparameter sensitivity: Llama-3-8B collapses to degeneracy at α=100 while Gemma models remain honest (Appendix G); requires careful per-model tuning
Representation drift explanation is correlational rather than causal; belief probing (Appendix E) is suggestive but not definitive evidence of causality
Experimental design choices lack strong justification: code length penalty value (0.003), layer filtering threshold (0.6), and follow-up prompt formulation appear ad-hoc
Continually retraining detector during RLVR doesn't improve honesty (Appendix L), suggesting fundamental limitation and reducing practical applicability
Limited novelty in positive results: finding that high KL + detector penalty yields honesty is somewhat expected; paper characterizes failure modes more than solving them
Presentation: 30-page paper with key results scattered across appendices; Figure 2 is dense; unclear whether white-box detectors outperform practical alternatives like human oversight
